To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have sequenced the complete coding sequence of a new HLA-DR serotype, DR 1405, which has never been reported.
we have sequenced a new DRB1 H allele and have identified three distinct groups of MHC class II molecules based on their cytoplasmic tail sequences.
we have cloned the complete DRB1 H1405 cDNA sequence, which has never been reported before, and that the cytoplamic domains of MHC class II gene products can be grouped into 3 different groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of HLA- DRB1 genes.
the cloning of the DRB1 H gene, and we have sequenced it.
the molecular basis of the genetic diversity of MHC molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DRB1 gene has a 1000 base pair coding region and a 200 base pair non-coding region.
the cytoplamic domain of DRB1 gene is not a constant region.
the DRB1 H locus is the most polymorphic of all HLA loci.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HLA- DRB1 H locus is a very dynamic gene locus with a high rate of mutation.
this is a report on complete coding region of DRB1 H1405, and a report of the three different cytoplasmic domains for the MHC class II gene products.
the DRB1 H alleles are more closely related to each other than the DRB3 H alleles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DRB1 H gene is a member of a family of genes with a conserved cytoplasmic region.
the cytoplamic domain is a potential source for allelic variation and may be a factor in the functional differences between alleles.
the DRB1*1401 allele is a rare allele.
